title: google_maps_flutter
objectives: Understand google_maps_flutter via a real-life analogy
Configure API keys + platform manifests correctly
Add markers, polylines, polygons, circles + custom info windows

Manage cost + attribution + Advanced Markers migration

sections.markdown:
**Think of `google_maps_flutter` as embedding a mini Google Maps app inside a Flutter widget.**

Unlike most Flutter widgets, GoogleMap is a **native view surface** — on Android it's a SurfaceView/TextureView hosting the Maps SDK; on iOS it's an MKMapView-styled UIView; on Web an iframe with the JS Maps API. Flutter composes it via a `PlatformView`. Everything you know about widgets — hot reload, Widget-tree rebuild, tests — has caveats around this surface.

- **API key required** — Google issues one per Android app + one per iOS bundle + one restricted to your Web domain. Ungoverned keys = billing horror stories.
- **Cost model** — Maps SDK is free up to $200 credit/month; overage bills per **map load** + per **direction request** + per **place autocomplete**. High-DAU consumer apps must monitor.
- **Advanced Markers** — new marker API (with better clustering + collision detection) replacing legacy `Marker` in 2024+. Migration ongoing.
- **Not everything Google Maps does is in the SDK** — Directions, Places, Roads are separate REST APIs consumed via HTTP calls; SDK renders the map + basic overlays.

**Why every logistics / delivery / discovery app uses this:** users expect the exact Google Maps UX (satellite, traffic, 3D, StreetView). Building a bespoke map UI is a multi-year project. Cost is the tension: budget it up front + tune (Lite mode, static maps for previews, capped autocomplete).

**`google_maps_flutter`** wraps the native Google Maps SDKs (Android, iOS, Web) as a Flutter widget. Renders the map as a `PlatformView`; exposes markers, polylines, polygons, circles, tile overlays, and a `GoogleMapController` (imperative API for camera control, projection, snapshot). Requires an API key per platform, enabled Maps SDK for Android / Maps SDK for iOS / Maps JS API in Google Cloud Console.

sections.markdown: ## Common mistakes

**Mistake 1: Unrestricted API key.** Copy-paste from a tutorial → leak in APK / Web bundle → attacker uses your quota. **Always restrict** in Google Cloud Console: Android key by SHA-1 + package; iOS by bundle ID; Web by referrer domain.

**Mistake 2: Rebuilding the GoogleMap widget on every state change.** PlatformView re-init is expensive (100-500 ms) + jarring. Isolate map state in its own widget/StatefulWidget; use markers/polylines via `Set` diffs.
**Mistake 3: Not batching marker updates.** 500 markers rebuilt one at a time thrashes the platform channel. Build the `Set<Marker>` once, then `setState`.
**Mistake 4: Ignoring cost.** Map loads at consumer scale rack up bills. Use **Lite mode** (Android) for lists of maps, **Static Maps API** for previews, cache Places autocomplete results.
**Mistake 5: Wrong permission wiring.** `myLocationEnabled: true` without runtime permission = silent failure. Request via `permission_handler` + `geolocator`.
**Mistake 6: Marker cluster storm.** 10 000 markers = frozen map. Use `google_maps_cluster_manager` or migrate to Advanced Markers with built-in clustering.

**Mistake 7: Info window UI limits.** Info windows are native raster; you can't put a Flutter widget inside. For rich UI, place a Flutter widget on top of the map via `Stack` + convert screen coords via `controller.getScreenCoordinate`.
**Mistake 8: Missing `dispose` on controller.** Leaks the map surface + memory. Always dispose in `State.dispose`.
## Best practices
**1. Restrict API keys.** Package + SHA-1 (Android), bundle ID (iOS), referrer (Web).
**2. Isolate map widget.** Wrap in a dedicated widget; parent state changes don't rebuild the PlatformView.
**3. Marker sets batched.** Compute once, apply once.
**4. Clustering for > 100 markers.**
**5. Use Static Maps for thumbnails / previews** — cheaper + faster.
**6. Lite mode for scrollable list of maps** — Android saves battery + CPU.
**7. Attribution + terms compliant** — Google requires their branding + logo visible; don't hide.
**8. Cost dashboards** — Google Cloud billing alert at $50 / $200; monitor per-day.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy)** — Show a map centered on user location; add a marker on tap.
**Practice 2 (Medium)** — Draw a route polyline between two points + animate camera to bounds.
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — Custom Flutter widget overlay tied to marker screen coord.
**Practice 4 (Hard)** — 5000 markers with `google_maps_cluster_manager` — verify perf.
**Practice 5 (Hard)** — Lite mode inside a scrollable list of shop cards.
**Practice 6 (Expert)** — Restrict API keys + set up Cloud billing alerts; simulate a keyless build to verify restriction works.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: How is Google Maps rendered inside a Flutter app?**

**A:** As a **PlatformView** — a native view surface embedded in the Flutter widget tree via `AndroidView` / `UiKitView`. On Android, it's a `MapView` (Google Maps SDK for Android); on iOS, a `GMSMapView` (Google Maps SDK for iOS); on Web, an iframe embedding the JS Maps API. Flutter's `GoogleMap` widget bridges via method channels — commands like `animateCamera` are serialized + sent to the native view; events (tap, camera move) come back. **Consequences:** (1) The map is NOT rendered by Skia / Impeller — it doesn't participate in Flutter's paint pipeline; (2) hot reload sometimes doesn't refresh map state; (3) placing Flutter widgets over the map works but they may flicker during heavy animations; (4) PlatformView init is expensive (~100-500 ms). **Rule:** treat the map as a heavy component; embed once; mutate via `GoogleMapController`.

**Q2: How do you keep Google Maps costs under control?**

**A:** **Cost model:** free $200/month credit; overage bills per map-load, per-Places-autocomplete, per-Directions-request. Levers: **(1) Static Maps** for previews (thumbnails in a card) — costs ~1/1000 of an interactive map load. **(2) Lite mode** on Android — static-like interactive map (no 3D / no gestures beyond pan/zoom) — cheaper + faster. **(3) Cache Places autocomplete** — dedupe recent queries locally, only hit API when new. **(4) Session tokens** for Places autocomplete — one billed session covers the typing + selection sequence. **(5) Cap Directions calls** — recompute only when destination changes. **(6) Cloud billing budget alerts** at $50 / $200 / $500. **(7) Monitor per-day usage** in Cloud Console; anomaly detection. **(8) Restrict keys** so a leaked key doesn't get exploited. **Sr interview signal:** knowing the specific SKUs + their per-1000 pricing.

**Q3: What's the cluster manager story for large marker sets?**

**A:** Rendering 5000 markers as individual `Marker`s tanks the map — every zoom triggers thousands of screen conversions. **Two options:** (1) **`google_maps_cluster_manager`** (community Flutter package) — groups markers by grid cell at the current zoom level + emits a single `Marker` per cluster with the item count. Zoom in → clusters split. (2) **Advanced Markers** (new SDK API, mid-2024 rollout) — built-in clustering with collision detection + custom cluster styles + PlatformView-optimized. **Migration path:** Advanced Markers eventually deprecate the legacy Marker; migrate when the flutter plugin support is stable. **Interview tip:** know that clustering exists — most candidates don't.

**Q4: How do you overlay a Flutter widget onto a marker (custom info window)?**

**A:** Info windows in the SDK are **native raster** — you can't put a Flutter widget inside. **Pattern:** (1) place your Flutter widget in a `Stack` over the map; (2) on marker tap, capture the marker's LatLng; (3) convert to screen coords via `controller.getScreenCoordinate(latLng)`; (4) `setState` to move the Flutter widget to those coords; (5) on camera move, listen via `onCameraMove` + re-convert. **Alternative:** on marker tap, show a `showModalBottomSheet` or floating card that's a full Flutter widget. Interviewers respect knowing the LIMITATION + the SDK's raster info-window vs the Flutter overlay pattern.

**Q5: How do you handle location permissions + user-location display?**

**A:** `myLocationEnabled: true` on the GoogleMap widget shows the blue dot + accuracy circle **IF** location permission is granted. Otherwise silently disabled. **Runtime:** (1) request via `permission_handler` (or `geolocator.checkPermission` + `requestPermission`); (2) also handle iOS 'When in Use' vs 'Always' distinction; Android's ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION vs COARSE. (3) React to permission changes at runtime — a user can revoke in Settings. **Manifests:** Android `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION" />`; iOS `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription` in Info.plist. **UX:** first-launch flow — explain WHY you need location (privacy rationale), then request. **Silent failure trap:** if permission denied, map still loads but no blue dot — devs think the plugin is broken. Log + surface UI: 'Enable location for map features.'

**Q6: What are the Web trade-offs?**

**A:** Web target uses the Maps JavaScript API loaded from Google's CDN. **Wins:** same widget API in Flutter code. **Caveats:** (1) API key must be **domain-restricted** in Cloud Console. (2) JS API pricing differs slightly from mobile SDK; check the per-load SKUs. (3) Not all APIs are 1:1 with mobile — some options fall back or no-op. (4) Loading the JS SDK adds ~150 KB gzipped to the app; consider lazy-load. (5) StreetView + advanced markers landed at different times on Web; check plugin support. (6) In `<iframe>` sandbox modes some features misbehave; test in prod-like host. (7) Attribution + Terms still enforced. **When Web parity matters:** consider Mapbox / Leaflet as alternatives — cheaper for high-DAU Web-first apps.

## Real-world usage

- **Delivery + logistics** — driver tracking, order handoff.
- **Discovery / listings** — restaurants, shops, listings on a map.
- **Route planning** — Directions API + Polyline.
- **Geofencing** — Circles / Polygons + native geofencing APIs.
- **NOT ideal for** — offline-only maps (use OSM / Mapbox); indoor floor plans (use Mapbox); high-DAU Web-first apps (consider MapLibre / Mapbox for cost).

## Advanced notes

- **Advanced Markers** — collision detection + higher-density rendering; migrate when Flutter plugin support stable.
- **Custom map styles** — Cloud-hosted styles via `MapId` in the console; SDK loads styled map without runtime JSON.
- **Traffic layer** — `trafficEnabled: true` — extra cost.
- **Indoor maps** — auto-shown for shopping malls / airports.
- **`controller.getVisibleRegion()`** — for viewport-driven queries (fetch pins in bounds).
- **`controller.getScreenCoordinate` / `.getLatLng`** — screen-to-map + inverse.
- **`snapshot()`** — bitmap capture, useful for share.
- **Marker icon customization** — `BitmapDescriptor.fromBytes` + custom-painted PNGs.
- **Google Places SDK / API** — separate; used for autocomplete + place details.
- **Directions API** — separate REST call; returns route polyline + waypoints.
- **Roads API** — snap-to-road for tracks.
- **Static Maps API** — server-rendered map image URL; cheapest for thumbnails.
- **Consumer alternatives** — Mapbox (better custom styling), OpenStreetMap via `flutter_map` (free but simpler feature set).
